title: Baited Live-Trapping of Triatomines in Semi-Arid Environments
author: Carezza Botto-Mahan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wnpfddn

steps.title: Select trapping locations
steps.instruction: Visually prospect areas likely to harbor triatomines, such as rocky outcrops, bromeliads, rock piles, animal burrows, etc., and choose suitable sites.

steps.title: Select bait according to season
steps.instruction: Choose bait based on season and time of day: during the hot season daytime use yeast; during the hot season nighttime use dry‑ice, a mouse, or yeast depending on weather; during the cold season use a mouse or dry‑ice.

steps.title: Prepare bait and assemble trap
steps.instruction: Prepare the selected bait and load it into the trap as follows:

substeps.instruction: Yeast bait: mix the ingredients inside the trapping device (B); add water only after reaching the final trap location to avoid spillover.
Dry‑ice bait: obtain ~200 g pieces of dry‑ice, cut them with a large knife and hammer while wearing eye goggles and thick gloves.

Mouse bait: place wood chips for bedding at the bottom of the trap, add a commercial mouse pellet and a fruit slice as food; introduce the mouse after the bedding and food are in place. Position the trap in a shaded, weather‑protected spot (under bushes, trees, rocks or cactuses).

steps.title: Place baited trap correctly
steps.instruction: Place the baited trap at its final point promptly, ensuring the trap stands upright, the upper margin of the trap (T) adheres to the chosen ecotope, and the trap surface is clean of dust to prevent climbing; note that some species (e.g., Rhodnius prolixus) can climb smooth surfaces.

steps.title: Set activation period and monitor
steps.instruction: Activate traps for the appropriate duration: for nocturnal triatomines, leave traps from sunset until the next morning; for diurnal triatomines, leave them from before midday until sunset, checking every 2–3 hours to avoid overheating, or alternatively set at sunset and retrieve around 12 am–2 pm to capture both diurnal and nocturnal insects.

steps.title: Inspect traps and collect insects
steps.instruction: When checking traps, inspect the entire trap including the bottom; use entomological forceps to grasp captured insects by the legs and transfer them into labeled plastic jars.

steps.title: Document capture data
steps.instruction: Record for each capture the trap ID, date, hour, species, developmental stage, and any other relevant information in both a field notebook and on the jar label.

steps.title: Handle and dispose of baits
steps.instruction: Manage used baits: discard remaining yeast mixture in a container or on the ground; dry‑ice will have sublimated; remove mice, place them in their maintenance cages, provide water and food, and protect them from extreme conditions during transport.

steps.title: Optional: add adhesive tape
steps.instruction: Optional: apply double‑sided adhesive tape to the outside of the trap near the bottom of compartment B to retain triatomines that attempt to climb, especially for Rhodniini.
